CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  September 15, 2026 - 5:00 P.M.
n  City Hall Council Chamber
  SPECIAL MEETING IN LIEU OF REGULAR MEETING
  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmember Jones)
  CLQSEDSESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the special meeting recessed at 5:01 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: Gabrieleno Band of Mission Indians - Kizh
  Nation v. Citv of Pasadena
  Case No.: LASC Case No. 26STCP02578

  Councilmember Jones
  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): One potential case
  arrived at the meeting at
  5:30 p.m.
  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding significant exposure to potential litigation pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): One potential case

  The above closed session item was not discussed.

  On the order of the Mayor, the special meeting reconvened at 6:16
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Cole.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  Interim City Manager Matthew E. Hawkesworth
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Police Commander Bill Grisafe introduced Sergeant Barry Glockson,
  as the new Sergeant At Arms. Sergeant Glockson thanked the City
  Council for the opportunity to serve in this capacity. Mayor Gordo

  Council Minutes  1  09/15/2026
   welcomed Sergeant Glockson and thanked Sergeant Adam Rosen
  for his service as the previous Sergeant At Arms to the City Council.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring September 21,
  2026 as Landscapers Appreciation Day in Pasadena, recognizing
  the vital contributions and skilled services provided by landscapers,
  with special recognition for the work performed after the Eaton Fire
  and windstorm. Jose Madera, Director of Pasadena Community Job
  Center, thanked the City Council for the recognition and encouraged
  the City Council to support state legislation to help gardeners
  transition from fossil-fuel-powered equipment to electric tools
  through grants or loans.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the month of
  October 2026 as First Tee - Greater Pasadena Month, and
  expressed his gratitude to First Tee - Greater Pasadena for
  enhancing the lives of youth through the game of golf. Ron
  Matthews, First Tee Board Member, and Bob Baderian, Executive
  Director, both accepted the proclamation on behalf of First Tee -
  Greater Pasadena and thanked the City Council and the Rose Bowl
  Operating Company for their long-standing partnership and support.

  Councilmember Jones requested that the meeting be adjourned in
  memory of Gerald Freeny, the first Black President of the
  Tournament of Roses, and spoke on his leadership and dedication
  to the Tournament and the City, spanning over three decades.

  Councilmember Cole also requested that the meeting be adjourned
  in memory of James Marrin, co-founder of Pasadena Heritage, and
  spoke on his passion for architecture and craftsmanship, and helping
  to preserve Pasadena and its architectural legacy.

  REPORTS AND  PROPOSED PASADENA MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENTS TO
  COMMENTS FROM  ESTABLISH A PILOT MICROENTERPRISE HOME KITCHEN
  CQUNCIL COMMITTEES  OPERATIONS (MEHKO) PROGRAM (Public Health Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  Economic Development  (1) Find that the proposed project referenced in the agenda report
  and Technology  is statutorily exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  Committee
  (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3)
  "Common Sense" exemption and categorically exempt pursuant to
  Section 15301 (Class 1, Existing Facilities), and there are no
  features that distinguish the project from others in the exempt
  classes, and therefore, there are not unusual circumstances, and no
  other exception to the exemption applies; and
  (2) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an ordinance within 60 days
  amending Title 8 of the Pasadena Municipal Code to establish a pilot
  Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations (MEHKO) Program for
  two years.

  Manuel Carmona, Public Health Director, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the item, providing information on the pilot program,
  potential impacts on economic development, and the role of
  Pasadena Public Health and associated costs.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding the
  estimated cost for the program, which increased from $175,000 to
  $225,000 since the project was previously presented to the EdTech
  Committee, Public Health Director Carmona reported that after
  reviewing all responsibilities to launch the program, City staff
  determined than an additional full-time employee would be needed
  to ensure the program was adequately staffed and functional.

  Council Minutes  8  09/15/2026
   In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the rationale
  for regulating MEKHOs differently from brick-and-mortar restaurants,
  Public Health Director Carmona spoke on disparities based on the
  volume of meals and noted that most MEHKOs are not serving full
  meals. He added that MEHKOs would be subject to applicable
  business-license requirements comparable to restaurants and would
  receive one inspection per year focused on the home kitchen.

  In response to Vice Mayor Rivas' inquiry regarding program funding,
  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth reported that the cost would
  need to be incorporated into the City's ongoing operating budget,
  and that the pilot program would provide more information about
  actual costs, program demands, and workload.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns regarding the
  MEHKO pilot program in terms of zoning implications, parking, sales
  tax collection, alcohol regulation, and public health oversight.

  Councilmember Masuda acknowledged concerns regarding the
  potential impact on existing restaurants, while expressing support for
  the proposed program and opportunities for new small businesses.

  The following individuals expressed support for MEHKOs, spoke on
  the program's positive impacts, emphasized the lack of negative
  impact on brick-and-mortar businesses, and/or provided other
  related comments:
  Richard Gomeztrejo, residence not stated
  Roger Overstreet, Pasadena resident
  Patrick Haugen, Pasadena resident
  Egor Chumak, residence not stated
  Elianne Rodriguez, Executive Director for LEAF
  Latoya Patillo, Pasadena resident
  Lauren Wolfer, Pasadena resident

  Strefan Fauble, Pasadena resident, expressed opposition to the
  implementation of MEHKO, and raised concerns regarding the
  program cost to applicant ratio and liability exposure for landlords
  if customers enter buildings for MEHKO related activities.

  Councilmember Cole expressed support for the equity elements
  behind the MEHKO program, while raising concerns regarding the
  cost of the program and future economic uncertainty.

  Councilmembers Hampton and Jones stated that MEHKOs may
  already be operating informally in the community and viewed the pilot
  program as an opportunity for residents to become legitimate
  businesses.

Council Minutes  9  09/15/2026
   ORIGINAL MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember hlampton, seconded by
  Councilmember Jones, to approve the staff recommendation,
  amended to add a one-year check-in to review the program's
n  progress and expenditures.

  Councilmember Madison expressed opposition to the proposed
  program, emphasizing concerns relating to neighborhood parking,
  the development ofADUs, impacts on the quality of life, and the need

  Discussion ensued regarding the funding cost of operating the pilot
  program, the promotion of small business opportunities and

  Mayor Gordo advocated for the item to return to the Economic

  Councilmember Cole requested that City staff reach out to other
  cities that have implemented MEHKO programs and gather
  feedback from their experiences.
